title: Gaussian Processes
interviewAnswer: A Gaussian process defines a distribution over functions using a mean and kernel; conditioning on observations produces a posterior predictive distribution with both mean and uncertainty.
why: GPs are canonical nonparametric probabilistic models and useful for small-data uncertainty-aware regression and Bayesian optimization.
intuition: Instead of fitting one curve, a GP reasons over many plausible functions and narrows uncertainty near observations.
deepDive: Every finite collection of function values is jointly Gaussian; the kernel defines covariance. Exact training solves an n×n covariance system and scales roughly O(n³).
commonMistakes: Saying GP means Gaussian input features.
production: Use GPs where calibrated local uncertainty matters and data size permits; monitor kernel fit and numerical conditioning.
workedExample: With an RBF kernel, uncertainty is narrow near data and widens far from observed inputs.
